title: Leaving the staff job; comparison with Basie
summary: Roy left because staff status meant nothing without playing, as with Basie's band.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Didn't you occasionally have a small group thing down there?
Not with me... Oh yeah! I don't think I got into that. Did you hear me playing on that?
I think there's one of "China Boy" or something...
It must have been Charlie Shavers.
No, it's you. But it's only about 16 bars or something.

I got out of there in a hurry, man. You know? Because what... So it's a big thing. So you're on staff. So what the hell does that mean? "Oh, yeah, I'm in the studio. I'm on staff." But if you ain't doin' nothin', hell, it ain't gonna mean nothin'. I'm not trying to impress nobody. I want to play.

Yeah, I'll (?) the same way I left Basie; you know, I went to Basie's band. Sit up there, doin' nothin' or... Hell, read music? I've been through that. I went over there because I thought I'd play some of them arrangements, you know, with Jo? Have some fun, you know. I didn't go over there to prove how much I could read. I did all of that!
Man, I very seldom got a chance to play with that band.
At the end of the night, he'd play "After You've Gone" after I didn't play no Jazz all night long.
